ri_new_beach_the.blurb: A short bouldering ledge in the Beach Pond state management area on the Rhode Island and Connecticut line, sitting a little off the trail among rhododendron woods. It holds 16 boulder problems with a wide spread: a handful of very easy lines and low-grade problems, a solid middle in the V1 to V3 range, and a few much harder ones up to V7 and V8. The rock is well textured and the setting is pleasant. Because it is so quick to reach, climbers use it as a warm-up stop on the way to the pond's southern boulders or as a destination for a short session.

ri_pedestal_boulder_the.blurb: A distinctive lone boulder balanced on smaller stones beside the paved park road in Lincoln Woods State Park, Rhode Island, on the Druid's Circle side across from the big split boulder. It has 16 boulder problems, from very easy up to V8, with a real concentration of hard climbing: several lines in the V5 to V7 range, including the three best-known problems at V5, plus a few mellow options at V0. It lies only a few steps off the pavement, so it is quick to reach and a handy place to meet up with others.

ut_cougar_crag.blurb: A small crag in Farmington Canyon in the northern Wasatch, a short walk of about five minutes from the car. It holds 16 routes and mixes styles: mostly traditional lines from 5.5 to 5.10, one sport route, plus a few winter ice routes from WI2 to WI4 and one M4 mixed line. It makes a quick evening outing in summer or winter, and the easy grades and brief approach suit newer climbers. It is a local crag rather than a destination, so a short session is all it is worth.
